```latex
\begin{remark}[Paper-II-E object-first export contract]
\label{p2e:rem:v2-conditional-export-contract}
\label{p2f:rem:v2-object-first-contract}
Every theorem below is stated first on the object it actually requires.  The
cone and Hopf exports use the derived compact parent and its Killing metric.
The projective, Hermitian-ray, commutant, and grading-weighted trace results
use the derived protected momentum summand
\(\mathcal S_{\rm prot}=V_{1/2,0}\oplus V_{0,1/2}\subset\mathcal H_p\cong\mathcal H_1\), imported from
Paper~II-B together with \(m_p=1\).  Its two chiral summands are co-realized
constituents; choosing one for a displayed branch calculation does not select
a physical chirality.  The current physical fixed-radius finite-coordinate
output is the generated class \(\mathsf C_D\), imported from Paper~II-C,
Corollaries~\ref{p2c:cor:intrinsic-coordinate-class-corealization}
and~\ref{p2c:cor:physical-fixed-radius-ancestry-exhaustion}.  The quoted
Paper-I-A coordinate normalization \(\mathsf C_{\rm PI}\) is instead an optional
representative inside the unresolved ambient completion atlas, while every
Hurwitz-support, vertex, diagonal, trimer, or \(15/24\) support statement is
on the core-support output \(\mathsf{Supp}_{2T}\).  Generic modules \(\mathcal H_m\) remain auxiliary
word-stage mathematics unless a later role separately constitutes them.
\end{remark}
```

```latex
\begin{remark}[Imported G0 export boundary]
All physical interfaces below are role-specific specializations of Paper~II-A's
stage-safe G0 certificate.  An asserted occurrence must exhibit a contingent
token of a geometrically licensed, claim-relative invariant distinction with
result-independent provenance; its tag alone supplies no witness or separate
actualization principle.  The generated geometric, momentum-carrier, and
fixed-radius \(\mathsf C_D\) lines of the object-first dependency chain are
structural theorem outputs; they require no duplicate occurrence witness.  A physical use
of a raw completion-dependent coordinate datum outside the generated
\(\mathsf C_D\) class, or of an ambient lift of that class,
a local occurrence of \(\mathsf{Supp}_{2T}\), any later causal/field
assignment, and every numerical normalization or readout not already generated
by \(\mathsf C_D\) require the
appropriate G0 occurrence or calibration certificate.  A new role, standard,
or comparison interface opens its own downstream dependency frontier; no
certificate reopens frozen upstream geometry.  G0 supplies their existence
typing but does not derive the witnesses.  Analytic requirements such as
prequantization integrality or regularity remain ordinary theorem-domain
conditions rather than consequences of G0.
\end{remark}
```

```latex
\begin{remark}[Displayed theorem-bank dependencies]
\label{p2:rem:kin-f-dependency-record}
The dependency chain is object-first:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \text{derived }SU(2)\text{ parent}+\text{Killing metric}
 &\Longrightarrow \text{cone, Hopf, and cotangent exports},\\
 \mathcal H_p\cong\mathcal H_1,\quad
 \mathcal S_{\rm prot}\subset\mathcal H_p
 &\Longrightarrow \text{projective, commutant, and trace results},\\
 \text{current fixed-radius momentum root}
 &\Longrightarrow \mathsf C_D
 \Longrightarrow (\mathrm{ND}_{\rm sp})
 \Longrightarrow \text{normalized protected }\Cl(0,3),\\
 +[\mathsf C]\text{ raw completion datum}
 &\Longrightarrow \text{raw completion-relative coordinate data and scales},\\
 +\bigl[(\mathrm{ND}_{\rm sp})\ \text{or an occurring nonzero
 protected-coordinate root/}\mathsf C_{\rm PI}\bigr]
 &\Longrightarrow \text{the normalized protected even }\Cl(0,3),\\
 +\bigl[\mathsf{Supp}_{2T}\text{ occurrence or a licensed
 support-to-core route}\bigr]
 &\Longrightarrow \text{the Hurwitz, trimer, and supported-trace consequences}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The compact carrier statements are Theorem~\ref{p2:thm:momentum-host-H1},
Theorem~\ref{p2b:thm:momentum-carrier-rigidity}, and
Corollary~\ref{p2b:cor:momentum-seed-constituent-corealization}.  The third
line is exactly the rooted generated image of
Corollaries~\ref{p2c:cor:intrinsic-coordinate-class-corealization}
and~\ref{p2c:cor:physical-fixed-radius-ancestry-exhaustion}; it removes the
nonvanishing premise on the current physical branch.  The raw ambient
coordinate-completion line nevertheless retains a genuine realization family.
On that larger atlas the nondegenerate protected-even line consumes the whole
nonzero family through the invariant output proved in
Corollaries~\ref{p2c:cor:nondegenerate-protected-clifford-orbit}
and~\ref{p2c:cor:protected-clifford-selector-discharge}, so it requires no
completion selector but still requires nonvanishing.  That predicate is also
redundant whenever the same claim contains an independently occurring nonzero
protected coordinate or the positive-normalized representative
\(\mathsf C_{\rm PI}\); otherwise the zero-member test preserves it as a
domain condition.  The exceptional-support line is generated from an occurring
root only on the licensed route of
Corollary~\ref{p2:cor:core-support-inheritance-no-duplicate-witness} or a
```

### BH-IIE-C-0009 — Normalized flat cone, homothety and commuting Hopf isometry

VERIFIED; Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex:387–412.

```latex
Let
\[

 \qquad
 C(S^3):=(0,\infty)\times S^3,
 \qquad
 \widetilde g:=dr^2+r^2g_E.
\]
The cone is isometric to \(\mathbb R^4\setminus\{0\}\), hence is flat and
hyper-K\"ahler.  Its radial field \(\rho=r\partial_r\) satisfies
\[
        \mathcal L_\rho\widetilde g=2\widetilde g.
\]
For the fixed Paper-I-A left-fiber Hopf representative, the
metric-normalized Reeb field \(\xi\) extends independently of \(r\) and obeys
\[
        \mathcal L_\xi\widetilde g=0,
        \qquad
        [\rho,\xi]=0.
\]
These are geometric homothety and isometry statements.  They do not define a
renormalization flow, Lorentzian time, or a gravitational field equation.
The controlling upstream results are Paper~I-A,
Theorem~\ref{p1:thm:hyperkahler-cone} and
Corollaries~\ref{p1:cor:flat-cone-canonical-scale}
and~\ref{p1:cor:flat-cone-four-density-homothety}.
```

### BH-IIE-C-0014 — Generator-normalized cotangent reduction

VERIFIED; Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex:536–568.

```latex
\begin{proposition}[Generator-normalized cotangent reduction]
\label{p2e:prop:normalized-cotangent-reduction}
At the metric-normalized moment level \(J_\xi=\mu\), one has
\[
        J_0=\mu_0:=\Rmom\mu.
\]
Cotangent reduction by the periodic circle action gives
\[
        J_0^{-1}(\mu_0)/U(1)\cong T^*S^2
\]
and, with \(\varepsilon_{\rm red}\in\{+1,-1\}\) recording the combined sign
convention for the canonical symplectic form, curvature, and left action,
\[
        \Omega_{\mathrm{red}}
        =\Omega_{\mathrm{can}}+\varepsilon_{\rm red}\mu_0\,\omega
        =\Omega_{\mathrm{can}}+\varepsilon_{\rm red}\Rmom\mu\,\omega.
\]
Fix the standard prequantum convention
\(F_{\nabla}=-i\Omega_{\mathrm{red}}/\hbar\) and the orientation
\([\omega/(2\pi)]\) used above.  Since \(\Omega_{\mathrm{can}}\) is exact,
the prequantum degree is
\[
        n_{\rm pq}
        =\varepsilon_{\rm red}\frac{\mu_0}{\hbar}
        =\varepsilon_{\rm red}\frac{\Rmom\mu}{\hbar}.
\]
Thus existence of the prequantum line is equivalent to
\[
        \frac{\mu_0}{\hbar}\in\mathbb Z,
        \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
        \frac{\Rmom\mu}{\hbar}\in\mathbb Z.
\]
\end{proposition}
```

```latex
\begin{proof}
The moment-map relation follows directly from
\(\xi=\xi_0/\Rmom\).  The standard cotangent-bundle reduction theorem for a
principal circle bundle adds the curvature term equal to the periodic
moment level times \(\omega\); the overall sign depends only on the declared
left-action and symplectic-form conventions and is retained as
\(\varepsilon_{\rm red}\).  Chern--Weil gives
\[
 c_1(L_{\rm pq})
 =\left[\frac{\Omega_{\rm red}}{2\pi\hbar}\right]
 =\varepsilon_{\rm red}\frac{\mu_0}{\hbar}
   \left[\frac{\omega}{2\pi}\right],
\]
because the canonical term is exact.  This proves both the signed degree and
the integrality condition.  Choosing the globally opposite convention would
reverse every degree simultaneously; it would not remove the relative factor
\(\varepsilon_{\rm red}\).
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{corollary}[Moment/prequantization joint zero-defect locus]
```

### BH-IIE-C-0020 — Celestial spinor--Hermitian-ray bridge

VERIFIED; Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex:740–814.

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Celestial spinor--Hermitian-ray bridge]
\label{p2e:thm:celestial-hermitian-ray-bridge}
For the already co-realized left chiral constituent, take the matching pair
\((SU(2)_L,S_L)\), with \(S_L\cong\mathbb C^2\), and let
\[
 \mathcal N_{\rm Herm}^{+}
 :=
 \{K\in\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C):
       K\ge0,\ \operatorname{rank}K=1\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Phi_L:\mathbb P(S_L)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal N_{\rm Herm}^{+}/\mathbb R_{>0},
 \qquad
 [z]\longmapsto[zz^\dagger],
\]
is a well-defined bijection.  Hence
\[
        \mathbb{CP}^1
        \cong
        \mathcal N_{\rm Herm}^{+}/\mathbb R_{>0}.
\]
Writing
\[
        K=k^\mu\sigma_\mu
        =k^0I+\sum_{i=1}^3k^i\sigma_i,
\]
one has
\[
        \det K=(k^0)^2-\lVert\mathbf k\rVert^2.
\]
For \(K=zz^\dagger\ne0\),
\[
        \det K=0,
        \qquad
        k^0=\frac12\operatorname{tr}K>0.
\]
The action
\[
        K\longmapsto A_LKA_L^\dagger,
        \qquad A_L\in SL(2,\mathbb C)_L,
\]
preserves the determinant and the future-positive component, and satisfies
\[
        (A_Lz)(A_Lz)^\dagger=A_L(zz^\dagger)A_L^\dagger.
\]
Its kernel is \(\{\pm I\}\), giving the standard isomorphism
\[
        PSL(2,\mathbb C)_L\cong SO^+(1,3).
\]
On the compact subgroup \(SU(2)_L\), \(k^0\) is fixed and
\(\mathbf k\) transforms through \(PSU(2)_L\cong SO(3)\).

For the right chiral pair \((SU(2)_R,S_R)\), regard
\(SL(2,\mathbb C)_R\) as a real Lie group and use its conjugate-dual
representation
\[
        z_R\longmapsto(A_R^\dagger)^{-1}z_R,
        \qquad A_R\in SL(2,\mathbb C)_R,
        \qquad
        K_R=z_Rz_R^\dagger
        \longmapsto
        (A_R^\dagger)^{-1}K_RA_R^{-1}.
\]
For each fixed \(A_R\), the spinor map is complex-linear and its
projectivization is holomorphic.  Its dependence on \(A_R\), however, is
antiholomorphic; it is not the holomorphic complexification of the defining
compact representation.  The Hermitian action is dual to
\(K\mapsto A_RKA_R^\dagger\) under the real pairing
\(\langle H,K\rangle=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(HK)\), and gives the dual
future-null-ray action.  On \(SU(2)_R\),
\((A_R^\dagger)^{-1}=A_R\), so it reduces to the matching
\(PSU(2)_R\cong SO(3)\) projective action.
\end{theorem}
```

Source proof, lines816–849:

```latex
\begin{proof}
Replacing \(z\) by \(cz\), \(c\ne0\), multiplies \(zz^\dagger\) by
\(|c|^2\), so the map is well defined.  Every nonzero positive rank-one
Hermitian matrix has the form \(zz^\dagger\).  For a fixed matrix the factor
is unique up to phase; after quotienting the matrix by
\(\mathbb R_{>0}\), the factor is unique up to an arbitrary nonzero complex
scalar.  This proves bijectivity.  The determinant identity
is the Pauli-matrix determinant formula.  The remaining statements follow
from \(\det(AKA^\dagger)=\det K\) for \(A\in SL(2,\mathbb C)\) and the
standard spin covering of the proper orthochronous Lorentz group.  The
right-chiral formulas follow by composing with the real Lie-group
automorphism
\[
 \vartheta(A):=(A^\dagger)^{-1},\qquad
 \vartheta(AB)=\vartheta(A)\vartheta(B),\qquad
 \vartheta^2=\operatorname{id}.
\]
Congruence by the invertible matrix \(\vartheta(A)\) preserves positivity,
rank, and determinant, so the same ray construction and covering kernel
apply.  For \(Z\in\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)\), viewed as a real Lie
algebra,
\[
 d\vartheta(Z)=-Z^\dagger,\qquad
 d\vartheta(iZ)=-i\,d\vartheta(Z).
\]
Thus the group-parameter map is antiholomorphic.  Its duality assertion is
the identity
\[
 \frac12\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
   (A^\dagger)^{-1}HA^{-1}\,AKA^\dagger\right]
 =\frac12\operatorname{tr}(HK),
 \qquad H,K\in\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C).
\]
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Conditional exceptional-role ancestry atlas]
\label{p2e:thm:joint-exceptional-core-support-ledger}
The finite exceptional support layer is role-indexed rather than one global
choice.  Its canonical outputs are
\[
 \mathsf{Supp}_{2T}=(\mathrm{core},[2T]),\qquad
 \mathsf{Supp}_{2O}=(\mathrm{normalizer/interface},[2O]),\qquad
 \mathsf{Supp}_{2I}=(\mathrm{perfect/global},[2I]).
\]
The following branches are licensed conditional entries.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2.2em]
\item A direct occurrence of one of these support roles supplies that role
without selecting a labelled representative.
\item An occurring point support supplies an exceptional descendant only
through an independently generated domain bridge and frozen exceptional
constructor; generic point resolution alone does not enter this atlas.
\item An occurring optimal regular \(24\)-cell generates the unmarked
\(\mathrm{GrpSupp}(2T)\) orbit by
Lemma~\ref{p2a:lem:v236-optimal24-recentering}.
\item An occurring \(\mathsf{QOp}_2\) role generates \([2T]\);
\(\mathsf{QOp}_3\) retains the unresolved pair \(\{[2O],[2I]\}\);
\(\mathsf{QOp}_{4,5}\) generates \([2I]\); and the corresponding
complete-band role is obstructed for \(m\ge6\), by
Theorem~\ref{p2a:thm:v236-qop-exceptional-frontier}.
\item If \(\mathsf{Supp}_{2O}\) occurs, its parent role remains active and
its group-word descendant satisfies \([2O,2O]=2T\); the generated tetrahedral
core is not a replacement for the octahedral normalizer/interface role.
\item If \(\mathsf{Supp}_{2I}\) occurs, the icosahedral parent remains
active.  Its five conjugate tetrahedral cores and their pairwise cyclic-axis
incidences are generated family data; choosing one core is an additional mark.
A least-core constructor may export the unmarked \([2T]\) class when that is
the consumed downstream role.
\item Scalar three- and five-torsion may generate
\(\mathrm{Abs/Tors}(2T)\) and \(\mathrm{Abs/Tors}(2I)\), respectively, but
these become physical momentum supports only after a typed same-owner
action/embedding bridge.
\item If a downstream claim consumes only the exact sampled band image and
transported operators, it may use \(\mathrm{Cmp}_m\) and requires no physical
exceptional point support.
\end{enumerate}
Thus no stronger exceptional parent is erased merely because it contains or
generates a tetrahedral core.  On every branch, all nonredundant unmarked
descendants are generated/co-realized; a vertex, diagonal, orientation,
performed support readout or selected trimer remains a token only when a
physical claim actually consumes it.
\end{theorem}
```

```latex
\begin{corollary}[Empty natural-\(2T\) module-identification locus]
\label{p2e:cor:empty-natural-2t-identification-locus}
The two natural \(2T\)-modules \(\mathcal H_1\) and
\(\mathcal E_{15}^{\rm BM}\) are separately admissible and both have complex
dimension \(15\).  Their natural fixed subspaces, however, have dimensions
\[
 \dim\mathcal H_1^{2T}=6,
 \qquad
 \dim(\mathcal E_{15}^{\rm BM})^{2T}=1.
\]
Consequently the joint locus obtained by adding a natural-\(2T\)-equivariant
isomorphism relation is empty:
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak Z_{\rm nat\text{-}iso}
 =
 \operatorname{Iso}_{2T}^{\rm nat}
   (\mathcal H_1,\mathcal E_{15}^{\rm BM})
 =\varnothing.}
\]
The equality of total dimensions supplies ordinary vector-space isomorphisms
but no distinguished map and no natural equivariant one.  In the absence of
the isomorphism relation, the two differently typed modules may co-realize by
relation-free composition.  Transporting one action through a separately
chosen vector-space isomorphism defines a different, map-dependent branch; it
does not repair the empty natural-action locus.
\end{corollary}
```

Source proof, lines1232–1238:

```latex
\begin{proof}
An equivariant isomorphism maps invariant vectors bijectively to invariant
vectors, so it would give an isomorphism between fixed subspaces and force
their dimensions to agree.  Since \(6\neq1\), no such map exists.  Ordinary
dimension equality forgets the action, and transporting the action changes
the relation being tested, proving the remaining clauses.
\end{proof}
```

### BH-IIE-C-0041 — First-order Hermitian trimer grammar

```latex
\begin{theorem}[First-order Hermitian trimer grammar]
\label{p2:thm:primitive-trimer-grammar}
In a cyclic vertex basis, define
\[
\DtriI=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac23,-\frac13,-\frac13\right),
\qquad
\DtriII=\operatorname{diag}(0,1,-1),
\]
\[
 C_1=X+X^\dagger,
 \qquad
 C_2=-i(X-X^\dagger).
\]
The first-order Hermitian slice is
\[
\mathfrak T_{\rm tri}
=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
\{I,\DtriI,\DtriII,C_1,C_2\}.
\]
Equivalently, every element of the slice has the form
\[
 H=\alpha I+\beta\DtriI+\gamma\DtriII+\rho C(\phi),
 \qquad
 C(\phi)=e^{-i\phi}X+e^{i\phi}X^2,
\]
with
\(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb R\),
\(\rho\ge0\), and
\(\phi\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)\).
\end{theorem}
```

### BH-IIE-C-0050 — Oriented-Hopf marked commutants

VERIFIED; Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex:1542–1571.

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Oriented-Hopf marked commutants]
\label{p2e:thm:oriented-hopf-marked-commutants}
Fix one oriented left-fibre Hopf representative, with the conventions of
Paper~II-D, Definition~\ref{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge},
and put \(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\).  At spin-cover level its stabilizer is
\(K_H=SU(2)_L\times U(1)_R\), and the protected restriction is
\[
 \mathcal S_{\rm prot}|_{K_H}
 =(\mathbf2)_0\oplus(\mathbf1)_{+1}\oplus(\mathbf1)_{-1}.
\]
Let \(P_R^{(\pm)}\) project onto the \(Q_H=\pm1\) right-handed
eigenlines, so \(P_R=P_R^{(+)}+P_R^{(-)}\).  Then
\[
 \boxed{\End_{K_H}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})
 =\mathbb CP_L\oplus\mathbb CP_R^{(+)}\oplus\mathbb CP_R^{(-)}
 \cong\mathbb C^3,}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\End_{K_H}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\rm sa}_0
 =\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\Gamma_{\rm sp},Q_H\},\qquad
 Q_H^2=P_R,\qquad\Gamma_{\rm sp}=I-2Q_H^2.}
\]
For the full level-one carrier the corresponding commutant is
\[
 \boxed{\End_{K_H}(\mathcal H_1)\cong
 M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathbb C^8.}
\]
These are pointwise commutants for the marked symmetry action, not
commutants of a covariant derivative.
\end{theorem}
```

```latex
\begin{proof}
The three protected summands displayed above are inequivalent irreducible
\(K_H\)-modules, so Schur's lemma gives their three scalar blocks.
The first has dimension two and the last two have dimension one.
Consequently \(\Gamma_{\rm sp}\) and \(Q_H\) span the two-dimensional
traceless Hermitian part.  The eigenvalues \(0,+1,-1\) give the two
polynomial identities.

Restricting the six summands of Paper~II-D,
Theorem~\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}, gives
\[
 \mathcal H_1|_{K_H}
 =2(\mathbf1)_0\oplus(\mathbf2)_0
 \oplus(\mathbf1)_{+1}\oplus(\mathbf1)_{-1}
 \oplus(\mathbf2)_{+1}\oplus(\mathbf2)_{-1}
 \oplus(\mathbf3)_0
 \oplus(\mathbf1)_{+2}\oplus(\mathbf1)_{-2}.
\]
The two copies of \((\mathbf1)_0\) come from \(V_{0,0}\) and the
zero Hopf weight of \(V_{0,1}\).  All eight other types occur once.
Schur's lemma therefore gives \(M_2(\mathbb C)\oplus\mathbb C^8\).
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Traceless refinement of the imported commutant]
\label{p2:thm:kin-u1-unique}
Define
\[
\End_{\Spin(4)}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\mathrm{sa}}_0
:=
\{Q\in\End_{\Spin(4)}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\mathrm{sa}}:
       \Tr_{\mathcal S_{\rm prot}}Q=0\}.

\[
\End_{\Spin(4)}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\mathrm{sa}}_0
=\mathbb R\Gamma_{\rm sp}.

\[
\End_{\Spin(4)}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\mathrm{sa}}_0
\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }
\End_{\Spin(4)}(\mathcal S_{\rm prot})^{\mathrm{sa}}/
\mathbb RI_{\mathcal S_{\rm prot}},
\qquad
q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp}
\longmapsto[q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp}].
\]
Thus every quotient class has the unique traceless representative
\(q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp}\).  A later real structure may orient the line, but
is not needed to derive it.
\end{theorem}
```

```latex
\begin{proposition}[Explicit protected-block grading-weighted traces]

\[

        \mathcal A_3(Q)=2(a^3-b^3).

\(Q=q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp}\),
\[
        \mathcal A_1(q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp})=4q_{\rm prot},
        \qquad
        \mathcal A_3(q_{\rm prot}\Gamma_{\rm sp})
        =4q_{\rm prot}^{\,3}.
\]

The factor \(2\) in both coefficients is
\(\rank P_L=\dim V_{(1/2,0)}=2\), the complex chiral-spinor dimension of each
protected summand.  It is therefore a spinor trace multiplicity at this stage,
not a Weyl-species count.  Only after a later Lorentzian Weyl interpretation
is supplied does the same factor become a Lorentz-spin trace normalization.  A species-normalized anomaly
coefficient counts one unit per Weyl species and would read \(a-b\) and
\(a^3-b^3\).  The two normalizations cannot be reconciled by rescaling the
charge, since \(Q\mapsto\lambda Q\) sends \(\mathcal A_1\mapsto\lambda\mathcal
A_1\) but \(\mathcal A_3\mapsto\lambda^3\mathcal A_3\).  The common zero locus
is unaffected, so the no-go statement below is independent of the choice.
\end{proposition}
```

```latex
\[
```

```latex
common kernel of the grading-weighted linear and cubic traces is
\[
 \boxed{
 \ker\mathcal A_1\cap\ker\mathcal A_3
 =\{aI_{\mathcal S_{\rm prot}}:a\in\mathbb R\}.}
\]

\(a\ne b\), lies in the common kernel.  On the traceless commutant line the
only common-kernel point is zero.  The surviving scalar line is vector-like
with respect to \(\Gamma_{\rm sp}\) and is not excluded by this finite trace
calculation.
Conditional on the physical chirality and gauged-\(U(1)\) identifications
stated above, this finite trace no-go becomes a perturbative anomaly
obstruction to a protected-only chirality-distinguishing generator.
\end{theorem}
```

```latex
the cubic trace also vanishes.  If \(Q\) is traceless, then
```

```latex
\begin{corollary}[Protected trace-free and chirality-distinguishing joint loci]

 =\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:
      2(a-b)=0,\ 2(a^3-b^3)=0\}
 =\{(t,t):t\in\mathbb R\}.}

\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak Z_{\rm eq}\cap\{(a,b):a\ne b\}=\varnothing.}
\]

\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak Z_{\rm tr}
 =\{q_{\rm prot}\in\mathbb R:
     4q_{\rm prot}=0,\ 4q_{\rm prot}^{\,3}=0\}
 =\{0\}.}
\]
Therefore adjoining an independently required nonzero traceless protected
generator gives the empty joint locus
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak Z_{\rm tr}\cap
        \{q_{\rm prot}\neq0\}=\varnothing.}
\]
Under the physical anomaly interpretation stated above, there is no
protected-only anomaly-free \(U(1)\) whose generator distinguishes the two
chiral constituents.  A scalar vector-like \(U(1)\) is not ruled out by these
two traces.  GP3 cannot select around the empty chirality-distinguishing locus.

fibre-product problem.  Writing their contributions as
\((B_1,B_3)\), the required equations are
\[
 4q_{\rm prot}+B_1=0,
 \qquad
 4q_{\rm prot}^{\,3}+B_3=0.
\]
Neither the existence of extra sectors nor either equation is generated by
the protected-block calculation.
\end{corollary}
```

### BH-IIE-C-0066 — Same-curvature line transfer is fixed by flat holonomy

VERIFIED; Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex:1967–1986.

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Same-curvature line transfer is fixed by flat holonomy]
\label{p2e:thm:v2210-lit-line-holonomy}
Let $L_1,L_2$ be Hermitian line bundles on the same connected base and
let $T:L_1\to L_2$ be a specified unitary bundle isomorphism.  Transport
$\nabla_1$ by $T$ and suppose it and $\nabla_2$ have the same curvature.
There is then a global real one-form $\alpha$ such that
\[
 \nabla_2-T\nabla_1T^{-1}=i\alpha,\qquad \mathrm d\alpha=0.
\]
For every closed loop $\gamma$,
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Hol}_{\nabla_2}(\gamma)}
 {\operatorname{Hol}_{T\nabla_1T^{-1}}(\gamma)}
 =\exp\left(-i\oint_\gamma\alpha\right).
\]
The two connections are gauge-equivalent exactly when all these ratios are
one, equivalently when every period of $\alpha$ belongs to $2\pi\mathbb Z$.
On a simply connected base, equality of curvature after the specified
bundle identification is sufficient.
\end{theorem}
```

Source proof, lines1987–1996:

```latex
\begin{proof}
Differences of unitary line connections are imaginary scalar one-forms,
and their curvature difference is $i\mathrm d\alpha$.  Parallel transport
of the difference along a loop gives the exponential.  If all periods are
integral multiples of $2\pi$, choose a base point and define the unitary
gauge by $\exp(-i\int\alpha)$; the period condition makes it independent
of the path and it transports the first connection to the second.
Conversely a unitary gauge has integral $2\pi$ periods and leaves loop
holonomies equal.  On a simply connected base a closed one-form is exact.
\end{proof}
```

```latex
\begin{theorem}[Ten local $S_3$ trimer fibres and their $A_2$ tangent planes]
\label{p2e:thm:v318-local-petersen-trimer}
On an occurring $2I$ packet, every vertex of the Petersen graph is a
threefold Hopf-axis line $[u_{ij}]$.  Its $A_5$ setwise stabilizer has
order six and is isomorphic to $S_3$; it permutes its three
Petersen neighbors faithfully.  Its real permutation module splits
canonically as $\mathbf1\oplus W_{A_2}$, with
\[
 W_{A_2}=\{(a,b,c)\in\mathbb R^3:a+b+c=0\},
 \qquad\dim W_{A_2}=2.
\]
With a representative axis and compatible cyclic orientations, the
Petersen cross-product directions $n_1,n_2,n_3\in u_{ij}^{\perp}$
form an $A_2$ root trimer and the map
$W_u=\sqrt{2/3}\,(n_1\ n_2\ n_3)$ satisfies
\[
 W_uW_u^{\mathsf T}=I_3-u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 W_u^{\mathsf T}W_u=I_3-\tfrac13J_3.
\]
Thus the local trimer-defect plane is isometric to the transverse
Hopf/Clifford tangent plane, conditional on its labelled frame.
This is not an automatic identification with the earlier one-core
$C_6^{\rm link}$, its $\mathbb C[Z_3]$ module, or the complex
fundamental color representation.
\end{theorem}
```

```latex
\begin{proof}
The stabilizer in $A_5$ of a two-label subset $\{i,j\}$ has
order $60/10=6$; for every permutation of the three unused labels
there is a unique parity-compatible permutation of the selected pair.
Hence its action on the three unused two-label combinations is all
$S_3$.  The permutation module decomposes into its constant
line and its standard $A_2$ plane.  The transverse identities are
the exact vector-projector identities of Paper~I-A, and the map
annihilates the constant line while preserving the inner product
on $W_{A_2}$.
\end{proof}
```

```json
          "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Generated Hopf normalization and character readout graphs]\n\\label{p2e:cor:joint-hopf-normalization-character-graphs}\nFor the fixed principal representative and the occurring radius\n\\(\\Rmom>0\\), the metric Hopf data form the generated graph\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\Gamma_{\\rm met}\n =\\left\\{\\left(\\xi_0,\\eta_0,\\Rmom;\\\n          \\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0,\\Rmom\\eta_0\\right)\\right\\}.}\n\\]\nThus \\(\\xi=\\Rmom^{-1}\\xi_0\\), \\(\\eta=\\Rmom\\eta_0\\), and\n\\(\\eta(\\xi)=1\\) are simultaneous outputs of one normalization dictionary, not\nthree independent assumptions.           "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Generator-normalized cotangent reduction]\n\\label{p2e:prop:normalized-cotangent-reduction}\nAt the metric-normalized moment level \\(J_\\xi=\\mu\\), one has\n\\[\n        J_0=\\mu_0:=\\Rmom\\mu.\n\\]\nCotangent reduction by the periodic circle action gives\n\\[\n        J_0^{-1}(\\mu_0)/U(1)\\cong T^*S^2\n\\]\nand, with \\(\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\in\\{+1,-1\\}\\) recording the combined sign\nconvention for the canonical symplectic form, curvature, and left action,\n\\[\n        \\Omega_{\\mathrm{red}}\n        =\\Omega_{\\mathrm{can}}+\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\mu_0\\,\\omega\n        =\\Omega_{\\mathrm{can}}+\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\Rmom\\mu\\,\\omega.\n\\]\nFix the standard prequantum convention\n\\(F_{\\nabla}=-i\\Omega_{\\mathrm{red}}/\\hbar\\) and the orientation\n\\([\\omega/(2\\pi)]\\) used above.  Since \\(\\Omega_{\\mathrm{can}}\\) is exact,\nthe prequantum degree is\n\\[\n        n_{\\rm pq}\n        =\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\frac{\\mu_0}{\\hbar}\n        =\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\frac{\\Rmom\\mu}{\\hbar}.\n\\]\nThus existence of the prequantum line is equivalent to\n\\[\n        \\frac{\\mu_0}{\\hbar}\\in\\mathbb Z,\n        \\qquad\\text{equivalently}\\qquad\n        \\frac{\\Rmom\\mu}{\\hbar}\\in\\mathbb Z.\n\\]\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe moment-map relation follows directly from\n\\(\\xi=\\xi_0/\\Rmom\\).  The standard cotangent-bundle reduction theorem for a\nprincipal circle bundle adds the curvature term equal to the periodic\nmoment level times \\(\\omega\\); the overall sign depends only on the declared\nleft-action and symplectic-form conventions and is retained as\n\\(\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\).  Chern--Weil gives\n\\[\n c_1(L_{\\rm pq})\n =\\left[\\frac{\\Omega_{\\rm red}}{2\\pi\\hbar}\\right]\n =\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\frac{\\mu_0}{\\hbar}\n   \\left[\\frac{\\omega}{2\\pi}\\right],\n\\]\nbecause the canonical term is exact.  This proves both the signed degree and\nthe integrality condition.  Choosing the globally opposite convention would\nreverse every degree simultaneously; it would not remove the relative factor\n\\(\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\).\n\\end{proof}"
        },

          "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Moment/prequantization joint zero-defect locus]\n\\label{p2e:cor:moment-prequantization-joint-locus}\nLet \\(\\mu\\in\\mathbb R\\) be the metric-normalized moment level,\n\\(\\mu_0\\in\\mathbb R\\) the periodic moment level, and\n\\(n_{\\rm pq}\\in\\mathbb Z\\) the degree of the standard prequantum line.  The\nlicensed generator transport and prequantization relation give, for each fixed\n\\(\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\in\\{+1,-1\\}\\), the exact joint locus\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm pq}^{(\\varepsilon_{\\rm red})}\n =\\left\\{(\\mu,\\mu_0,n_{\\rm pq}):\n     \\mu_0=\\Rmom\\mu\n     =\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\hbar n_{\\rm pq},\\\n     n_{\\rm pq}\\in\\mathbb Z\\right\\}.}\n\\]\nEquivalently, it is the graph\n\\[\n n_{\\rm pq}\\longmapsto\n \\left(\\frac{\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\hbar n_{\\rm pq}}{\\Rmom},\n       \\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\hbar n_{\\rm pq},n_{\\rm pq}\\right).\n\\]\nIt therefore selects no integer and no occurring moment level.  For an\nindependently supplied \\(\\mu\\), the fibre is a singleton precisely when\n\\(\\Rmom\\mu/\\hbar\\in\\mathbb Z\\), and is empty otherwise; on the nonempty fibre,\n\\(n_{\\rm pq}=\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\Rmom\\mu/\\hbar\\).  If the prequantum line\nis explicitly identified, with the same orientation and Chern convention,\nwith the Hopf-associated line \\(L^{n_{\\rm H}}\\), the same-object relation forces\n\\(n_{\\rm pq}=n_{\\rm H}\\); absent that line identification, equality of the two\ninteger labels may not be inserted merely because both lie in \\(\\mathbb Z\\).\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe moment-map dictionary gives \\(\\mu_0=\\Rmom\\mu\\), while the preceding\nproposition gives\n\\(n_{\\rm pq}=\\varepsilon_{\\rm red}\\mu_0/\\hbar\\).  Solving these two\nequations gives the displayed graph.  Fixing \\(\\mu\\) then\ngives the stated singleton/empty alternative.  The final clause is the typed\nsame-line relation; equality of unbridged integer owner slots would be a\nrelation and typing insertion.\n\\end{proof}"
        },

Its full projectivization is\n\\(\\mathbb P(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\\cong\\mathbb{CP}^3\\), while either already\nco-realized chiral constituent may be used branchwise and projectivizes to\n\\(\\mathbb{CP}^1\\).         "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Joint chiral-factor/constituent typing locus]\n\\label{p2e:thm:joint-chiral-typing-locus}\nConsider the formal enumeration atlas\n\\[\n \\{SU(2)_L,SU(2)_R\\}\\times\\{S_L,S_R\\}.\n\\]\nFor the matching-factor role, in which the acting factor must act in its\ndefining chiral representation, the complete joint\nGP1/zero-GP2-defect locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm chir}\n =\\{(SU(2)_L,S_L),(SU(2)_R,S_R)\\}.}\n\\]\nThe crossed tuples are not further physical alternatives: \\(SU(2)_L\\) acts\ntrivially on \\(S_R=V_{0,1/2}\\), and \\(SU(2)_R\\) acts trivially on\n\\(S_L=V_{1/2,0}\\), so either crossed tuple has a typing/relation defect for the\ndeclared defining-action role.  Both surviving pairs are nonredundant generated\nconstituents of the already occurring\n\\(\\Spin(4)\\)-protected composite and therefore co-realize.  Selecting one pair\nfor a branchwise formula is not a physical chirality selector.\n\nMoreover, \\(\\mathbb P(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\\cong\\mathbb{CP}^3\\) and\n\\(\\mathbb P(S_\\chi)\\cong\\mathbb{CP}^1\\) occupy full-protected and\nbranchwise-projective sorts.  No cross tuple identifying the whole\n\\(\\mathbb{CP}^3\\) with one celestial \\(\\mathbb{CP}^1\\) is admissible: their\ncomplex dimensions are \\(3\\) and \\(1\\).  A later physical chirality assignment\nmust therefore be an independently generated bridge to one of the two\nco-realized branch pairs.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nBy definition of \\(V_{j_L,j_R}\\), the left factor acts in the defining\ntwo-dimensional representation exactly when \\(j_L=1/2\\), and the right factor\ndoes so exactly when \\(j_R=1/2\\).  This gives the two matching tuples and makes\nthe opposite-factor action trivial on each crossed constituent.  Paper~II-A's\ngenerated-constituent no-omission rule retains both nonredundant matches in the\nfull protected composite.  The projective dimension calculation is\n\\(\\dim_{\\mathbb C}\\mathbb P(\\mathbb C^n)=n-1\\), giving \\(3\\neq1\\) and hence\nthe final type obstruction.\n\\end{proof}",

        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Celestial spinor--Hermitian-ray bridge]\n\\label{p2e:thm:celestial-hermitian-ray-bridge}\nFor the already co-realized left chiral constituent, take the matching pair\n\\((SU(2)_L,S_L)\\), with \\(S_L\\cong\\mathbb C^2\\), and let\n\\[\n \\mathcal N_{\\rm Herm}^{+}\n :=\n \\{K\\in\\operatorname{Herm}_2(\\mathbb C):\n       K\\ge0,\\ \\operatorname{rank}K=1\\}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n \\Phi_L:\\mathbb P(S_L)\\longrightarrow\n \\mathcal N_{\\rm Herm}^{+}/\\mathbb R_{>0},\n \\qquad\n [z]\\longmapsto[zz^\\dagger],\n\\]\nis a well-defined bijection.  Hence\n\\[\n        \\mathbb{CP}^1\n        \\cong\n        \\mathcal N_{\\rm Herm}^{+}/\\mathbb R_{>0}.\n\\]\nWriting\n\\[\n        K=k^\\mu\\sigma_\\mu\n        =k^0I+\\sum_{i=1}^3k^i\\sigma_i,\n\\]\none has\n\\[\n        \\det K=(k^0)^2-\\lVert\\mathbf k\\rVert^2.\n\\]\nFor \\(K=zz^\\dagger\\ne0\\),\n\\[\n        \\det K=0,\n        \\qquad\n        k^0=\\frac12\\operatorname{tr}K>0.\n\\]\nThe action\n\\[\n        K\\longmapsto A_LKA_L^\\dagger,\n        \\qquad A_L\\in SL(2,\\mathbb C)_L,\n\\]\npreserves the determinant and the future-positive component, and satisfies\n\\[\n        (A_Lz)(A_Lz)^\\dagger=A_L(zz^\\dagger)A_L^\\dagger.\n\\]\nIts kernel is \\(\\{\\pm I\\}\\), giving the standard isomorphism\n\\[\n        PSL(2,\\mathbb C)_L\\cong SO^+(1,3).\n\\]\nOn the compact subgroup \\(SU(2)_L\\), \\(k^0\\) is fixed and\n\\(\\mathbf k\\) transforms through \\(PSU(2)_L\\cong SO(3)\\).\n\nFor the right chiral pair \\((SU(2)_R,S_R)\\), regard\n\\(SL(2,\\mathbb C)_R\\) as a real Lie group and use its conjugate-dual\nrepresentation\n\\[\n        z_R\\longmapsto(A_R^\\dagger)^{-1}z_R,\n        \\qquad A_R\\in SL(2,\\mathbb C)_R,\n        \\qquad\n        K_R=z_Rz_R^\\dagger\n        \\longmapsto\n        (A_R^\\dagger)^{-1}K_RA_R^{-1}.\n\\]\nFor each fixed \\(A_R\\), the spinor map is complex-linear and its\nprojectivization is holomorphic.  Its dependence on \\(A_R\\), however, is\nantiholomorphic; it is not the holomorphic complexification of the defining\ncompact representation.  The Hermitian action is dual to\n\\(K\\mapsto A_RKA_R^\\dagger\\) under the real pairing\n\\(\\langle H,K\\rangle=\\tfrac12\\operatorname{tr}(HK)\\), and gives the dual\nfuture-null-ray action.  On \\(SU(2)_R\\),\n\\((A_R^\\dagger)^{-1}=A_R\\), so it reduces to the matching\n\\(PSU(2)_R\\cong SO(3)\\) projective action.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nReplacing \\(z\\) by \\(cz\\), \\(c\\ne0\\), multiplies \\(zz^\\dagger\\) by\n\\(|c|^2\\), so the map is well defined.  Every nonzero positive rank-one\nHermitian matrix has the form \\(zz^\\dagger\\).  For a fixed matrix the factor\nis unique up to phase; after quotienting the matrix by\n\\(\\mathbb R_{>0}\\), the factor is unique up to an arbitrary nonzero complex\nscalar.  This proves bijectivity.  The determinant identity\nis the Pauli-matrix determinant formula.  The remaining statements follow\nfrom \\(\\det(AKA^\\dagger)=\\det K\\) for \\(A\\in SL(2,\\mathbb C)\\) and the\nstandard spin covering of the proper orthochronous Lorentz group.  The\nright-chiral formulas follow by composing with the real Lie-group\nautomorphism\n\\[\n \\vartheta(A):=(A^\\dagger)^{-1},\\qquad\n \\vartheta(AB)=\\vartheta(A)\\vartheta(B),\\qquad\n \\vartheta^2=\\operatorname{id}.\n\\]\nCongruence by the invertible matrix \\(\\vartheta(A)\\) preserves positivity,\nrank, and determinant, so the same ray construction and covering kernel\napply.  For \\(Z\\in\\mathfrak{sl}(2,\\mathbb C)\\), viewed as a real Lie\nalgebra,\n\\[\n d\\vartheta(Z)=-Z^\\dagger,\\qquad\n d\\vartheta(iZ)=-i\\,d\\vartheta(Z).\n\\]\nThus the group-parameter map is antiholomorphic.  Its duality assertion is\nthe identity\n\\[\n \\frac12\\operatorname{tr}\\!\\left[\n   (A^\\dagger)^{-1}HA^{-1}\\,AKA^\\dagger\\right]\n =\\frac12\\operatorname{tr}(HK),\n \\qquad H,K\\in\\operatorname{Herm}_2(\\mathbb C).\n\\]\n\\end{proof}",
        "scope": "Nonzero complex spinors modulo C*, positive rank-one Hermitian matrices modulo positive real scaling; left holomorphic and right real-group branches kept separate.",
        "replay_steps": [
          "For z→cz, zz†→|c|²zz†. Spectral factorization of each nonzero positive rank-one Hermitian matrix supplies a spinor unique up to phase; quotient by positive scale supplies the projective bijection.",
          "Expand K=k0I+kiσi; the Pauli determinant is k0²−|k|². For rank one PSD K, determinant vanishes and k0=tr(K)/2>0.",
          "Congruence by A∈SL2(C) preserves Hermiticity, positivity, rank and determinant. Spinor congruence intertwining follows by associativity.",
          "The invoked standard spin covering SL2(C)→SO+(1,3) has kernel ±I. On SU2, trace is preserved and the spatial action is the rotation quotient.",
          "θ(A)=(A†)^−1 satisfies θ(AB)=θ(A)θ(B), θ²=id. Since dθ(Z)=−Z†, dθ(iZ)=−i dθ(Z): antiholomorphic dependence on group parameter. Each fixed matrix still acts complex linearly on spinors.",
          "The right duality identity follows by cancellation and cyclicity: tr[(A†)^−1HA^−1 AKA†]=tr(HK). On SU2, (A†)^−1=A, so the compact action matches."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [

Paper~II-E does not\nidentify this cone with a physical tangent-space causal cone, derive a\nnoncompact transport group, or produce finite-dimensional unitary boost\ndynamics. The branchwise constructions do not by themselves constitute a\nsingle physical \\(\\Spin(1,3)\\) action on \\(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}\\).  In\nparticular,\n\\[\n \\boxed{S_L\\oplus S_R\\text{ co-realizes}\\not\\Longrightarrow\\text{a physically selected Lorentz chirality or boost/transport law}.}\n\\]\nA later paper may compose one branch with an independently derived Lorentzian\ncausal cone; that composition and any physical chirality assignment are not\npremises of the present theorem.\n\\end{remark}",

        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Generated fixed-radius protected branch]\n\\label{p2e:cor:generated-fixed-radius-protected-branch}\nOn the current physical fixed-radius momentum branch, the finite-coordinate\nessential image is the singleton \\(\\{\\mathsf C_D\\}\\).  In the raw-atlas\ncoordinates its exact tuple is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n (r_{1,0},r_{0,1},\\varrho_{\\rm sp})_D\n =\\left(\\frac{\\sqrt2\\Rmom}{3},\n        \\frac{\\sqrt2\\Rmom}{3},\n        \\frac{\\sqrt3\\Rmom}{4}\\right).}\n\\]\nConsequently every allowed finite edge is nonzero and\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n (\\mathrm{ND}_{\\rm sp})\\ \\text{holds},\\qquad\n \\sum_{a=1}^4(X_a^{\\rm sp})^2\n =\\frac{3\\Rmom^2}{4}I_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}.}\n\\]\nThe normalized protected even algebra is therefore the represented\n\\(\\Cl(0,3)\\) without an additional nondegeneracy or completion-selection\npremise.  This conclusion selects no ambient lift, POVM, prepared state,\nHamiltonian, or numerical calibration, and \\(\\mathsf C_D\\ne\\mathsf C_{\\rm cone}\\).\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:intrinsic-tangential-coordinate-class}, gives\nthe displayed tuple, its nonzero-edge statement, and the protected quadratic\nfingerprint.  Paper~II-C,\nCorollary~\\ref{p2c:cor:intrinsic-coordinate-class-corealization}, supplies the\nrooted constructor word, while\nCorollary~\\ref{p2c:cor:physical-fixed-radius-ancestry-exhaustion} proves that\nits physical essential image is exactly \\(\\{\\mathsf C_D\\}\\).  Since\n\\(\\Rmom>0\\), the value \\(\\sqrt3\\Rmom/4\\) is nonzero, and substitution into\n\\(4\\varrho_{\\rm sp}^{2}I\\) gives \\(3\\Rmom^2I/4\\).\nCorollaries~\\ref{p2c:cor:nondegenerate-protected-clifford-orbit}\nand~\\ref{p2c:cor:protected-clifford-selector-discharge} then give the\nnormalized represented \\(\\Cl(0,3)\\).  Their typed target excludes the listed\nambient, apparatus, state, and dynamical data, so none is inherited.\n\\end{proof}",

        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Completion-independent protected even algebra]\n\\label{p2e:cor:protected-clifford-selector-discharge}\nOn the nondegenerate protected stratum\n\\[\n (\\mathrm{ND}_{\\rm sp}):\\qquad \\varrho_{\\rm sp}>0,\n\\]\ndefine \\(Y_a:=\\varrho_{\\rm sp}^{-1}X_a^{\\rm sp}\\) and, for\n\\(i=1,2,3\\), \\(e_i:=Y_iY_4\\).  Paper~II-C,\nCorollaries~\\ref{p2c:cor:nondegenerate-protected-clifford-orbit}\nand~\\ref{p2c:cor:protected-clifford-selector-discharge}, give\n\\[\n e_i=C_iC_4,\\qquad\n e_i^2=-I,\\qquad\n e_ie_j+e_je_i=-2\\delta_{ij}I,\n\\]\nand therefore\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\operatorname{alg}_{\\mathbb R}(I,e_1,e_2,e_3)\n =\\operatorname{alg}_{\\mathbb R}(I,C_1C_4,C_2C_4,C_3C_4)\n \\cong\\Cl(0,3).}\n\\]\nThus every compatible finite completion with \\(\\varrho_{\\rm sp}>0\\) gives the\nsame represented normalized protected even algebra.  Selecting\n\\(\\mathsf C_{\\rm PI}\\), a numerical value of the positive protected magnitude,\nor a relative chiral phase is not required for this output.  On the bare\ncompletion atlas, the antecedent \\((\\mathrm{ND}_{\\rm sp})\\) remains a genuine\nnonvanishing domain condition and fixes neither raw coordinate coefficients,\nan absolute radius, an ambient lift, nor the coordinate--coordinate commutator\nmagnitude.\n\\end{corollary}",

        "evidence_id": "IIE-RP-009",

        "title": "Joint protected-nondegeneracy discharge",
        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          979,

        ],
        "claim_label": "p2e:cor:joint-protected-nondegeneracy-discharge",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Joint discharge boundary for protected nondegeneracy]\n\\label{p2e:cor:joint-protected-nondegeneracy-discharge}\nOn the generated fixed-radius \\(\\mathsf C_D\\) branch,\nCorollary~\\ref{p2e:cor:generated-fixed-radius-protected-branch} discharges\n\\((\\mathrm{ND}_{\\rm sp})\\) without any additional occurrence or calibration\npremise.  More generally, if a physical claim independently contains an\noccurring protected-coordinate\nvector whose frozen distinction is \\(X^{\\rm sp}\\neq0\\), and the licensed\nrelation identifies it with the protected block of the raw completion, then\n\\[\n X^{\\rm sp}\\neq0\n \\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n \\varrho_{\\rm sp}>0.\n\\]\nThe joint zero-defect completion locus is therefore the positive stratum, and\na separate \\((\\mathrm{ND}_{\\rm sp})\\) premise is redundant for that claim.\nThe same discharge holds when the occurring representative is\n\\(\\mathsf C_{\\rm PI}\\), since\n\\(\\rho_{\\rm prot}>0\\) and\n\\(\\varrho_{\\rm sp}=\\rho_{\\rm prot}/2\\).\n\nIf neither a nonzero protected-coordinate occurrence nor an occurring\npositive-normalized representative is present, the zero completion\n\\(\\alpha=\\beta=0\\) preserves all frozen relations and closure obligations that\ndo not explicitly require the protected edge.         "scope": "Alternative typed antecedents: generated C_D; independently occurring nonzero protected vector identified with raw block; positive C_PI representative; otherwise bare raw atlas.",
        "replay_steps": [

          "The zero example is confined to raw atlas branches; it is not a counterexample to the already generated C_D branch."

        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\item Scalar three- and five-torsion may generate\n\\(\\mathrm{Abs/Tors}(2T)\\) and \\(\\mathrm{Abs/Tors}(2I)\\), respectively, but\nthese become physical momentum supports only after a typed same-owner\naction/embedding bridge.\n\\item If a downstream claim consumes only the exact sampled band image and\ntransported operators, it may use \\(\\mathrm{Cmp}_m\\) and requires no physical\nexceptional point support.\n\\end{enumerate}\nThus no stronger exceptional parent is erased merely because it contains or\ngenerates a tetrahedral core.  On every branch, all nonredundant unmarked\ndescendants are generated/co-realized; a vertex, diagonal, orientation,\nperformed support readout or selected trimer remains a token only when a\nphysical claim actually consumes it.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nBranches (i)--(iii) are the direct, bridged and optimal-support constructions\nof Paper~II-A, including its orbit-level recentering lemma.  Branch (iv) is\nTheorem~\\ref{p2a:thm:v236-qop-exceptional-frontier}; in particular full\nquadratic sampling alone is insufficient unless the finite operation and\nrole-faithful comparison content of \\(\\mathsf{QOp}_2\\) is present.  Paper~I-B\nsupplies the intrinsic exceptional group identities\n\\([2O,2O]=2T\\), the five tetrahedral subgroups of \\(2I\\), and the scalar\nthree-/five-torsion abstract realizations.  GP2 no-insertion enforces the\nsame-owner bridge on branch (vii), while\nProposition~\\ref{p1b:prop:v233-sampling-restriction} gives branch (viii) on\nthe exact comparison image.  Generated-constituent no-omission retains each\nnonredundant parent and descendant role.\n\\end{proof}",
        "scope": "Symplectic scalar torsion automorphism/frame-torsor sorts versus embedded momentum support; exact band-image comparison only.",
        "replay_steps": [
          "I-B scalar p-torsion F_p² with alternating form has symplectic automorphism group SL2(F_p); at p3 and p5 this is abstractly 2T and 2I.",

          "For exact subgroup samplers, scaled restriction R S_Γ=S_Γ′ is unitary on sampled band images and transports band operators; no full point-support data is inferred.",
          "Constituent no-omission retains licensed descendants but does not actualize arbitrary labelled members."
        ],

        "claim_label": "p2e:prop:bm-supported-trace-boundary",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Bose--Mesner supported trace and natural-action boundary]\n\\label{p2e:prop:bm-supported-trace-boundary}\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:s3one-numerical-data}, provides the orthogonal\ncommon-space decomposition~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}\n\\[\n \\mathbb C^{2T}\n =\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\oplus\\mathcal E_9^{\\rm BM}.\n\\]\nFor the inclusion\n\\(\\iota_{15}:\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\hookrightarrow\\mathbb C^{2T}\\),\ndefine, without suppressing their carriers,\n\\[\n \\tau_{24}(A):=\\frac1{24}\\Tr_{\\mathbb C^{2T}}A,\n \\qquad\n \\tau_{15}(B):=\\frac1{15}\\Tr_{\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}}B.\n\\]\nThese normalized traces satisfy the equivalent identities\n\\[\n \\tau_{24}\\!\\left(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*\\right)\n =\\frac{15}{24}\\,\\tau_{15}(B),\n \\qquad\n \\tau_{15}(B)\n =\\frac{24}{15}\\,\n  \\tau_{24}\\!\\left(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*\\right),\n \\qquad\n B\\in\\End(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}).\n\\]\nFor the natural left-\\(2T\\) actions used in Paper~I-A, there is no equivariant\nisomorphism\n\\[\n        \\mathcal H_1\\cong\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}.\n\\]\nNo such restriction is asserted for arbitrary vector-space isomorphisms or\nfor actions transported through a separately chosen isomorphism.\nThe natural-action statement is precisely Paper~I-A,\nProposition~\\ref{p1:prop:h1-e15-left-2t-obstruction}.\n\\end{proposition}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nBecause \\(\\iota_{15}\\) is an isometric inclusion,\n\\[\n \\Tr_{\\mathbb C^{2T}}(\\iota_{15}B\\iota_{15}^*)\n =\\Tr_{\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}}B.\n\\]\nDividing the left side by \\(24\\) and the right side by \\(15\\) proves the\nfirst trace identity; algebraic inversion proves the second.  The natural\nleft-\\(2T\\) equivariance obstruction is proved separately in\nPaper~II-F, Section~\\ref{p2e:app:natural-action-no-go}.\n\\end{proof}",
        "scope": "One actual orthogonal 15-dimensional summand of the 24-dimensional regular scalar function space; B any endomorphism of that summand.",
        "replay_steps": [
          "I-A BM decomposition yields E15⊕E9 orthogonally in C^(2T). Isometric inclusion satisfies iota* iota=I15.",
          "Cyclicity on compatible rectangular maps gives Tr24(iota B iota*)=Tr15(B). Dividing gives tau24=(15/24)tau15 and reciprocal tau15=(24/15)tau24.",
          "No positivity/Hermiticity of B is needed; the trace equality holds for every complex endomorphism.",

        "claim_label": "p2e:cor:empty-natural-2t-identification-locus",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Empty natural-\\(2T\\) module-identification locus]\n\\label{p2e:cor:empty-natural-2t-identification-locus}\nThe two natural \\(2T\\)-modules \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) and\n\\(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM}\\) are separately admissible and both have complex\ndimension \\(15\\).  Their natural fixed subspaces, however, have dimensions\n\\[\n \\dim\\mathcal H_1^{2T}=6,\n \\qquad\n \\dim(\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM})^{2T}=1.\n\\]\nConsequently the joint locus obtained by adding a natural-\\(2T\\)-equivariant\nisomorphism relation is empty:\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm nat\\text{-}iso}\n =\n \\operatorname{Iso}_{2T}^{\\rm nat}\n   (\\mathcal H_1,\\mathcal E_{15}^{\\rm BM})\n =\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nThe equality of total dimensions supplies ordinary vector-space isomorphisms\nbut no distinguished map and no natural equivariant one.  In the absence of\nthe isomorphism relation, the two differently typed modules may co-realize by\nrelation-free composition.  Transporting one action through a separately\nchosen vector-space isomorphism defines a different, map-dependent branch; it\ndoes not repair the empty natural-action locus.\n\\end{corollary}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nAn equivariant isomorphism maps invariant vectors bijectively to invariant\nvectors, so it would give an isomorphism between fixed subspaces and force\ntheir dimensions to agree.  Since \\(6\\neq1\\), no such map exists.  Ordinary\ndimension equality forgets the action, and transporting the action changes\nthe relation being tested, proving the remaining clauses.\n\\end{proof}",
        "scope": "Natural SU2_L restriction of H1 and natural left regular action on the BM summand.",
        "replay_steps": [
          "I-A fixed-space proof: trivial left factors (0,0),(0,1/2),(0,1) give 1+2+3=6 invariants in H1; defining V2 and rotation V3 contribute none.",
          "The regular scalar target has only constants invariant, and the constant eigenvector belongs to E15, giving one invariant there.",
          "An equivariant isomorphism restricts to a bijection of invariant spaces; 6≠1 refutes that relation. Equal total dimensions alone give only nondistinguished vector-space isomorphisms.",
          "Action transport through a chosen vector-space isomorphism changes the natural-action branch, so it is not a counterexample to emptiness."
        ],

The two objects are\ndistinct generated descendants of the unmarked core role.         "source_lines": [
          1336,
          1363
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[Kinematic cyclic trimer template]\n\\label{p2:prop:kinematic-cyclic-trimer-template}\nLet \\(T\\) be either oriented Paper-I-A trimer and let \\(X\\) be its\norientation-preserving cyclic shift.  Then \\(T\\) is a free transitive\n\\(Z_3\\)-set and\n\\[\n E_T:=\\mathbb C^T\\cong\\mathbb C[Z_3]\n \\cong\\mathbf1\\oplus\\chi\\oplus\\chi^{-1},\n \\qquad\n \\chi(X)=e^{2\\pi i/3}.\n\\]\nOn the underlying real permutation module,\n\\[\n        \\mathbb R^T\\cong\\mathbb R\\oplus W,\n        \\qquad\n        \\dim_{\\mathbb R}W=2,\n\\]\nand the pair module has\n\\[\n        \\dim_{\\mathbb C}(E_T\\otimes E_T^*)=9.\n\\]\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1359,
          "end_line": 1363,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThese are the regular-representation and trimer-pair support statements of\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Complex regular Z3 trimer module, real standard plane and pair module",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Either oriented Paper-I-A trimer with orientation-preserving cyclic shift",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0040",
        "replay_steps": [
          "An oriented trimer has exactly three vertices; its orientation-preserving shift X has one orbit of length three, hence the Z3 action is free and transitive.",
          "Its complex permutation module is the regular representation of Z3. Discrete Fourier vectors furnish the trivial, chi, and inverse-chi lines. Reversing basis convention can exchange the latter two without changing the direct sum.",
          "Over the reals the constant vector spans R; its orthogonal sum-zero subspace W has real dimension two and carries the 120-degree rotation.",
          "The complex trimer-pair module E_T tensor E_T^* has dimension 3 times 3 = 9."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [
          "p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar",
          "p1:cor:finite-trimer-pair-supports"
        ],
        "condition_predicates_for_canonical_match": [

      "id": "BH-IIE-EV-B2-E1G-005",

        "audit_id": "BH-IIE-C-0041",

        "labels": [

        ],
        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1365,
          1399
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[First-order Hermitian trimer grammar]\n\\label{p2:thm:primitive-trimer-grammar}\nIn a cyclic vertex basis, define\n\\[\n\\DtriI=\\operatorname{diag}\\!\\left(\\frac23,-\\frac13,-\\frac13\\right),\n\\qquad\n\\DtriII=\\operatorname{diag}(0,1,-1),\n\\]\n\\[\n C_1=X+X^\\dagger,\n \\qquad\n C_2=-i(X-X^\\dagger).\n\\]\nThe first-order Hermitian slice is\n\\[\n\\mathfrak T_{\\rm tri}\n=\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\n\\{I,\\DtriI,\\DtriII,C_1,C_2\\}.\n\\]\nEquivalently, every element of the slice has the form\n\\[\n H=\\alpha I+\\beta\\DtriI+\\gamma\\DtriII+\\rho C(\\phi),\n \\qquad\n C(\\phi)=e^{-i\\phi}X+e^{i\\phi}X^2,\n\\]\nwith\n\\(\\alpha,\\beta,\\gamma\\in\\mathbb R\\),\n\\(\\rho\\ge0\\), and\n\\(\\phi\\in\\mathbb R/(2\\pi\\mathbb Z)\\).\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1396,
          "end_line": 1399,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThis is Paper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}, restated\nin Paper-II notation~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Five-dimensional first-order Hermitian trimer slice",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Cyclic vertex basis; X cyclic shift; alpha,beta,gamma real; rho>=0; phi modulo 2pi",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0041",
        "replay_steps": [
          "Since X^3=I and X is a unitary permutation, X^dagger=X^2. C1=X+X^dagger and C2=-i(X-X^dagger) are Hermitian.",
          "The three real diagonal Hermitian directions are spanned by I, DtriI, DtriII, with DtriI and DtriII independent trace-zero diagonals.",
          "C1 and C2 are independent off-diagonal Hermitian directions; their support is disjoint from the diagonal subspace, giving real dimension five.",
          "For aC1+bC2 choose rho=sqrt(a^2+b^2) and phi with a=rho cos(phi), b=rho sin(phi). Then rho C(phi)=rho(e^(-i phi)X+e^(i phi)X^2). At rho=0 arbitrary phi represents the same zero vector, and the target asserts existence only.",
          "This is the first-order slice retaining one cyclic transport orbit, as explicitly defined in I-A; it is not asserted to be the full Hermitian algebra or a physical closure algebra."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [
          "p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar"

        ],

        "candidate_issues": [],

        "source_lines": [
          1401,
          1435
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Kinematic trimer Weyl and \\(A_2\\) defect constants]\n\\label{p2:cor:kinematic-trimer-weyl-a2}\nLet \\(\\omega=e^{2\\pi i/3}\\), \\(Ze_j=\\omega^je_j\\), and\n\\(Xe_j=e_{j+1}\\).  Then\n\\[\n X^3=Z^3=I,\n \\qquad\n ZX=\\omega XZ,\n\\]\nand the nine operators \\(X^aZ^b\\), \\(a,b\\in\\mathbb Z_3\\), form a\ntrace-orthogonal basis of \\(M_3(\\mathbb C)\\).  For\n\\(D_j=P_j-I/3\\),\n\\[\n \\operatorname{tr}(D_j^2)=\\frac23,\n \\qquad\n \\operatorname{tr}(D_iD_j)=-\\frac13\n \\quad(i\\ne j).\n\\]\nFor \\(\\alpha_1=P_0-P_1\\) and \\(\\alpha_2=P_1-P_2\\),\n\\[\n\\operatorname{tr}(\\alpha_i\\alpha_j)\n=\n\\begin{pmatrix}\n2&-1\\\\\n-1&2\n\\end{pmatrix}_{ij}.\n\\]\nThus the resulting defect plane is the \\(A_2\\) root/weight plane.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1431,
          "end_line": 1435,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThese are the Paper-I-A finite Weyl and trimer-defect identities following from\nTheorem~\\ref{p1:thm:cyclic-trimer-operator-grammar}\n\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Finite Weyl basis and trace-metric A2 defect plane",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "X e_j=e_(j+1); Z e_j=omega^j e_j; indices mod3",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0042",
        "replay_steps": [
          "On e_j, ZX e_j=omega^(j+1)e_(j+1)=omega XZ e_j. The order-three identities follow from the periodic basis and omega^3=1.",
          "For W_ab=X^a Z^b, tr(W_ab^dagger W_cd)=3 delta_(a,c) delta_(b,d): if shifts differ there are no diagonal entries; if shifts agree, the trace is the finite Fourier sum. Thus the nine operators are a Hilbert-Schmidt trace-orthogonal basis of M3(C).",
          "With tr(P_iP_j)=delta_ij and tr(I)=3, tr((P_j-I/3)^2)=1-2/3+1/3=2/3, and for i!=j the cross trace is 0-1/3-1/3+1/3=-1/3.",
          "For alpha1=P0-P1 and alpha2=P1-P2 the diagonal norms are 2 and cross inner product is -1, exactly the printed A2 Cartan Gram matrix.",
          "The roots and centered projectors lie in the same real trace-zero diagonal plane; the root/weight-plane descriptor does not identify their different integral lattices."
        ],

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Imported Paper-I-A protected commutant]\n\\label{p2:prop:kin-u1-commutant}\nPaper~I-A, Theorem~\\ref{p1:thm:s3one-commutant-line}, proves that the\ncomplex-linear commutant and its Hermitian part are~\\cite{Kugelmann2026a}\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\n=\\mathbb CP_L\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R\n=\\mathbb CI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\oplus\\mathbb C\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\n\\]\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}\n=\\mathbb RP_L\\oplus\\mathbb RP_R\n=\\mathbb RI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\oplus\\mathbb R\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}.\n\\]\nPaper~II-E uses this as an imported theorem and does not re-prove the Schur\ndecomposition.\n\\end{theorem}",

        "source_lines": [
          1504,
          1528
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Finite antipodal lifts on the protected block]\n\\label{p2e:cor:protected-antipodal-lifts}\nLet\n\\[\n z_L=(-I,I),\\qquad z_R=(I,-I),\\qquad z_c=(-I,-I)\n\\]\nas in Paper~II-D.  On\n\\(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}=V_{\\frac12,0}\\oplus V_{0,\\frac12}\\),\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\rho(z_L)=-\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\\qquad\n        \\rho(z_R)=+\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},\\qquad\n        \\rho(z_c)=-I_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}.}\n\\]\nThus a provenance-fixed Hopf half-turn may coincide, up to the inherited\nhanded sign, with the protected grading as a finite involution.  This does not\nidentify the infinitesimal Hopf generator with \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and does\nnot select a nonzero gauged abelian generator.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1523,
          "end_line": 1528,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nOn \\(V_{\\frac12,0}\\), \\(z_L\\) acts by \\(-1\\) and \\(z_R\\) by \\(+1\\); on\n\\(V_{0,\\frac12}\\) the signs are reversed.  Writing the resulting diagonal\noperators in terms of \\(P_L,P_R\\) gives the first two identities, and their\nproduct gives the third.\n\\end{proof}"

          1542,

        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Oriented-Hopf marked commutants]\n\\label{p2e:thm:oriented-hopf-marked-commutants}\nFix one oriented left-fibre Hopf representative, with the conventions of\nPaper~II-D, Definition~\\ref{p2:def:finite-diagonal-spin-weight-hopf-charge},\nand put \\(Q_H:=Q_{H,L}=-2L_3^-\\).  At spin-cover level its stabilizer is\n\\(K_H=SU(2)_L\\times U(1)_R\\), and the protected restriction is\n\\[\n \\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}|_{K_H}\n =(\\mathbf2)_0\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-1}.\n\\]\nLet \\(P_R^{(\\pm)}\\) project onto the \\(Q_H=\\pm1\\) right-handed\neigenlines, so \\(P_R=P_R^{(+)}+P_R^{(-)}\\).  Then\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})\n =\\mathbb CP_L\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R^{(+)}\\oplus\\mathbb CP_R^{(-)}\n \\cong\\mathbb C^3,}\n\\]\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\rm sa}_0\n =\\operatorname{span}_{\\mathbb R}\\{\\Gamma_{\\rm sp},Q_H\\},\\qquad\n Q_H^2=P_R,\\qquad\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}=I-2Q_H^2.}\n\\]\nFor the full level-one carrier the corresponding commutant is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\End_{K_H}(\\mathcal H_1)\\cong\n M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8.}\n\\]\nThese are pointwise commutants for the marked symmetry action, not\ncommutants of a covariant derivative.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1573,
          "end_line": 1594,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThe three protected summands displayed above are inequivalent irreducible\n\\(K_H\\)-modules, so Schur's lemma gives their three scalar blocks.\nThe first has dimension two and the last two have dimension one.\nConsequently \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and \\(Q_H\\) span the two-dimensional\ntraceless Hermitian part.  The eigenvalues \\(0,+1,-1\\) give the two\npolynomial identities.\n\nRestricting the six summands of Paper~II-D,\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:diagonal-center-grading}, gives\n\\[\n \\mathcal H_1|_{K_H}\n =2(\\mathbf1)_0\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{+1}\\oplus(\\mathbf2)_{-1}\n \\oplus(\\mathbf3)_0\n \\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{+2}\\oplus(\\mathbf1)_{-2}.\n\\]\nThe two copies of \\((\\mathbf1)_0\\) come from \\(V_{0,0}\\) and the\nzero Hopf weight of \\(V_{0,1}\\).  All eight other types occur once.\nSchur's lemma therefore gives \\(M_2(\\mathbb C)\\oplus\\mathbb C^8\\).\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "type_signature": "Marked K_H protected/full-H1 commutants",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Oriented left-fibre mark; Q_H=-2L3^-; K_H=SU2_L x U1_R",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B2-RG-0050",
        "replay_steps": [
          "With Q_H=-2L3^- the left protected doublet is an SU2_L doublet of weight zero, and the right doublet splits into SU2_L singlets of weights +1 and -1. These three K_H types are pairwise inequivalent.",
          "Schur gives C P_L direct sum C P_R^(+) direct sum C P_R^(-). Its Hermitian trace-zero part has coefficients (a,b,c) satisfying 2a+b+c=0 and is spanned by Gamma_sp and Q_H.",
          "Q_H eigenvalues (0,0,+1,-1) yield Q_H^2=P_R and I-2Q_H^2=Gamma_sp.",
          "Restrict the six H1 Spin(4) types: V00 gives (1)_0; V_(1/2,0) gives (2)_0; V_(0,1/2) gives (1)_+1+(1)_-1; V_(1/2,1/2) gives (2)_+1+(2)_-1; V_(1,0) gives (3)_0; V_(0,1) gives (1)_+2+(1)_0+(1)_-2.",
          "Combining equal types yields two copies of (1)_0 and eight other multiplicity-one types. Their total dimension is 2+2+1+1+2+2+3+1+1=15. The commutant is M2(C) direct sum C^8 (complex dimension 12).",
          "These are pointwise symmetry-action commutants. No covariant derivative or holonomy centralizer has been substituted."

        "source_label": "p2:thm:kin-u1-unique",
        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "statement_source_lines": [
          1618,
          1645
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Traceless refinement of the imported commutant]\n\\label{p2:thm:kin-u1-unique}\nDefine\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n:=\n\\{Q\\in\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}:\n       \\Tr_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}Q=0\\}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n=\\mathbb R\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}.\n\\]\nThe quotient map restricts to an isomorphism\n\\[\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}_0\n\\xrightarrow{\\ \\cong\\ }\n\\End_{\\Spin(4)}(\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot})^{\\mathrm{sa}}/\n\\mathbb RI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}},\n\\qquad\nq_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\n\\longmapsto[q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}].\n\\]\nThus every quotient class has the unique traceless representative\n\\(q_{\\rm prot}\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\).  A later real structure may orient the line, but\nis not needed to derive it.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "Hermitian unmarked Spin(4)-equivariant operators on S_prot=V_(1/2,0)⊕V_(0,1/2), with ranks2+2.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1647,
          1658

        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nBy the Paper-I-A commutant theorem imported in\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:prop:kin-u1-commutant},\n\\(Q=aP_L+bP_R\\) with \\(a,b\\in\\mathbb R\\). The common zero locus\nis unaffected, so the no-go statement below is independent of the choice.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "All real a,b in Q=aP_L+bP_R, protected spinor trace of rank2+2 blocks.",
        "proof_source_lines": [

        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nUse\n\\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}P_L=P_L\\),\n\\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}P_R=-P_R\\),\n\\(\\Tr P_L=\\Tr P_R=2\\), and\n\\(P_LP_R=0\\).         "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Protected-block trace kernel and chirality-distinguishing no-go]\n\\label{p2:thm:protected-anomaly-no-go}\nAmong all Hermitian \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariant generators \\(Q=aP_L+bP_R\\), the complete\ncommon kernel of the grading-weighted linear and cubic traces is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\ker\\mathcal A_1\\cap\\ker\\mathcal A_3\n =\\{aI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}:a\\in\\mathbb R\\}.}\n\\]\nConsequently no chirality-distinguishing generator, equivalently no point with\n\\(a\\ne b\\), lies in the common kernel.  On the traceless commutant line the\nonly common-kernel point is zero.  The surviving scalar line is vector-like\nwith respect to \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) and is not excluded by this finite trace\ncalculation.\nConditional on the physical chirality and gauged-\\(U(1)\\) identifications\nstated above, this finite trace no-go becomes a perturbative anomaly\nobstruction to a protected-only chirality-distinguishing generator.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "All Hermitian Spin(4)-equivariant Q=aP_L+bP_R on protected block; physical perturbative obstruction only under declared interpretation.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1804,
          1811
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nProposition~\\ref{p2:prop:protected-anomaly-traces} gives\n\\(\\mathcal A_1(Q)=2(a-b)\\).  Hence\n\\(\\mathcal A_1(Q)=0\\) implies \\(a=b\\), and then \\(Q=aI_{\\mathcal S_{\\rm prot}}\\);\nthe cubic trace also vanishes.  If \\(Q\\) is traceless, then\n\\(2(a+b)=4a=0\\), so \\(Q=0\\).  Equivalently, on the traceless line the\ndisplayed grading-weighted traces vanish only for \\(q_{\\rm prot}=0\\).\n\\end{proof}",

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Protected trace-free and chirality-distinguishing joint loci]\n\\label{p2e:cor:protected-anomaly-free-joint-locus}\nOn the full Hermitian \\(\\Spin(4)\\)-equivariant commutant, the joint zero locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm eq}\n =\\{(a,b)\\in\\mathbb R^2:\n      2(a-b)=0,\\ 2(a^3-b^3)=0\\}\n =\\{(t,t):t\\in\\mathbb R\\}.}\n\\]\nIts intersection with the chirality-distinguishing stratum is empty:\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\rm eq}\\cap\\{(a,b):a\\ne b\\}=\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nOn the protected traceless commutant line, the same classification reduces to\n\\[\n \\boxed{\n \\mathfrak Z_{\\rm tr}\n =\\{q_{\\rm prot}\\in\\mathbb R:\n     4q_{\\rm prot}=0,\\ 4q_{\\rm prot}^{\\,3}=0\\}\n =\\{0\\}.}\n\\]\nTherefore adjoining an independently required nonzero traceless protected\ngenerator gives the empty joint locus\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\mathfrak Z_{\\rm tr}\\cap\n        \\{q_{\\rm prot}\\neq0\\}=\\varnothing.}\n\\]\nUnder the physical anomaly interpretation stated above, there is no\nprotected-only anomaly-free \\(U(1)\\) whose generator distinguishes the two\nchiral constituents.  A scalar vector-like \\(U(1)\\) is not ruled out by these\ntwo traces.  GP3 cannot select around the empty chirality-distinguishing locus.\n\nIf additional chiral matter sectors occur, cancellation is a new joint\nfibre-product problem.  Writing their contributions as\n\\((B_1,B_3)\\), the required equations are\n\\[\n 4q_{\\rm prot}+B_1=0,\n \\qquad\n 4q_{\\rm prot}^{\\,3}+B_3=0.\n\\]\nNeither the existence of extra sectors nor either equation is generated by\nthe protected-block calculation.\n\\end{corollary}",

Intersecting the scalar kernel with\n\\(a\\ne b\\), or the traceless singleton with the nonzero stratum, is empty.\nTrace additivity gives the two displayed equations for an enlarged matter\nrepresentation, which must be solved on that representation's actual typed\ncharge atlas.\n\\end{proof}",

        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Oriented-Hopf protected weighted trace-zero locus]\n\\label{p2e:thm:marked-hopf-weighted-trace-locus}\nOn the marked domain of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2e:thm:oriented-hopf-marked-commutants}, write\n\\[\n T=aP_L+b_+P_R^{(+)}+b_-P_R^{(-)},\\qquad a,b_+,b_-\\in\\mathbb R.\n\\]\nFor the same grading-weighted functionals\n\\(\\mathcal A_k(T)=\\Tr(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}T^k)\\), \\(k=1,3\\), one has\n\\[\n \\mathcal A_1(T)=2a-b_+-b_-,\\qquad\n \\mathcal A_3(T)=2a^3-b_+^3-b_-^3,\n\\]\nand the exact common zero locus is\n\\[\n \\boxed{\\{T:\\mathcal A_1(T)=\\mathcal A_3(T)=0\\}\n =\\mathbb RI\\ \\cup\\ \\mathbb RQ_H.}\n\\]\nIts ordinary-traceless part is exactly \\(\\mathbb RQ_H\\).\nThis is a union of two lines, not their linear span.\nIt changes the invariance group of\nTheorem~\\ref{p2:thm:protected-anomaly-no-go} and therefore leaves that\nunmarked theorem intact.  The spacetime-chirality and internal-charge\nidentifications required for a physical anomaly interpretation remain\nseparate; splitting geometric magnetic weights does not supply them.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "scope": "Oriented-Hopf marked K_H commutant: ranks2,1,1 and real a,b+,b−.",
        "proof_source_lines": [
          1894,
          1902
        ],
        "proof_as_printed": "\\begin{proof}\nThe ranks of \\(P_L,P_R^{(+)},P_R^{(-)}\\) are \\(2,1,1\\), respectively,\nand \\(\\Gamma_{\\rm sp}\\) acts on them as \\(+1,-1,-1\\), proving the\ntrace formulas.  The first zero condition gives \\(b_\\pm=a\\pm d\\).\nSubstitution into the cubic gives \\(\\mathcal A_3=-6ad^2\\).  Over\n\\(\\mathbb R\\) the alternatives are \\(d=0\\), giving \\(T=aI\\), or\n\\(a=0\\), giving \\(T=dQ_H\\).  Their ordinary traces are \\(4a\\) and zero,\nso only \\(\\mathbb RQ_H\\) survives ordinary tracelessness.\n\\end{proof}",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The same Γ has eigenvalue+1 on rank2 left block and−1 on each rank1 right line, giving A1=2a−b+−b− and A3=2a³−b+³−b−³.",

          "On the locus ordinary trace is4a, so its traceless slice is exactlyRQ_H.",

        "claim_id": "BH-IIE-C-0066",

        "labels": [
          "p2e:thm:v2210-lit-line-holonomy"
        ],
        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1967,
          1996
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Same-curvature line transfer is fixed by flat holonomy]\n\\label{p2e:thm:v2210-lit-line-holonomy}\nLet $L_1,L_2$ be Hermitian line bundles on the same connected base and\nlet $T:L_1\\to L_2$ be a specified unitary bundle isomorphism.  Transport\n$\\nabla_1$ by $T$ and suppose it and $\\nabla_2$ have the same curvature.\nThere is then a global real one-form $\\alpha$ such that\n\\[\n \\nabla_2-T\\nabla_1T^{-1}=i\\alpha,\\qquad \\mathrm d\\alpha=0.\n\\]\nFor every closed loop $\\gamma$,\n\\[\n \\frac{\\operatorname{Hol}_{\\nabla_2}(\\gamma)}\n {\\operatorname{Hol}_{T\\nabla_1T^{-1}}(\\gamma)}\n =\\exp\\left(-i\\oint_\\gamma\\alpha\\right).\n\\]\nThe two connections are gauge-equivalent exactly when all these ratios are\none, equivalently when every period of $\\alpha$ belongs to $2\\pi\\mathbb Z$.\nOn a simply connected base, equality of curvature after the specified\nbundle identification is sufficient.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 1987,
          "end_line": 1996,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nDifferences of unitary line connections are imaginary scalar one-forms,\nand their curvature difference is $i\\mathrm d\\alpha$.  Parallel transport\nof the difference along a loop gives the exponential.  If all periods are\nintegral multiples of $2\\pi$, choose a base point and define the unitary\ngauge by $\\exp(-i\\int\\alpha)$; the period condition makes it independent\nof the path and it transports the first connection to the second.\nConversely a unitary gauge has integral $2\\pi$ periods and leaves loop\nholonomies equal.  On a simply connected base a closed one-form is exact.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "type_signature": "Unitary line connections with specified unitary bundle identification",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Same connected smooth base; T given; equal transported curvatures",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0066",
        "evidence_level": "E1",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "replay_steps": [
          "The specified unitary isomorphism T places both connections on the same Hermitian line. Their difference is a globally defined imaginary scalar one-form i alpha.",
          "For line connections the curvature difference is i d alpha; equal curvature gives d alpha=0.",
          "The parallel-transport equation for the difference yields Hol2/Hol1=exp(-i integral_loop alpha), with the sign matching the declared connection difference.",
          "If every period is 2pi times an integer, g(x)=exp(-i integral_(x0 to x) alpha) is single-valued and satisfies g nabla1 g^-1=nabla1+i alpha=nabla2.",
          "Conversely a U1-valued gauge changes its phase by integer multiples of 2pi around loops, so all holonomy ratios are one. On a simply connected smooth base, a closed real one-form is exact."
        ],
        "consumed_imports": [],

        "E3_claimed": false
      },
      "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED"

        "source_file": "Paper2E-KinematicExports-v3_130.tex",
        "source_lines": [
          1998,
          2012
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{corollary}[Equal degrees do not identify every native charge owner]\n\\label{p2e:cor:v2210-lit-degree-versus-phase}\nOn the actual Hopf base $S^2$, aligned orientation, the supplied line\nisomorphism and equal curvature suffice to identify the transported phase\nconnection up to gauge.  Equal Chern degree alone fixes neither the\ncurvature representative nor that isomorphism.  On $M_8$, even equal\ncurvature can leave a flat phase difference on its two scalar circles.\n\\end{corollary}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2006,
          "end_line": 2012,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nApply the preceding theorem and $H^1(S^2;\\mathbb R)=0$.  The supplied\nproduct has $H_1(M_8;\\mathbb Z)=\\mathbb Z^2$; flat unitary differences\ncan therefore have independent holonomies on the two scalar generators.\nEquality of Chern degree concerns the integral curvature class, not a\npointwise curvature form or these flat holonomies.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",

        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0067",
        "evidence_level": "E1",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",

        "replay_steps": [
          "S2 is simply connected and H1(S2;R)=0. Under the supplied bundle isomorphism, equal curvature makes the connection difference exact and hence gauge removable.",

          "The supplied M8 product is (S1 times S3)^2; Kunneth gives H1(M8;Z)=Z^2. A flat difference alpha=a dtheta1+b dtheta2 has independent loop phases exp(-2pi i a),exp(-2pi i b).",

          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nApply Theorem~\\ref{p2c:thm:v226-chirality-radius} to the protected projector\nand the inherited chirality sign. Reversing orientation exchanges the two\nstates and leaves the bound unchanged.\n\\end{proof}"
```
