        "source_lines": [
          2089,
          2124
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{theorem}[Ten local $S_3$ trimer fibres and their $A_2$ tangent planes]\n\\label{p2e:thm:v318-local-petersen-trimer}\nOn an occurring $2I$ packet, every vertex of the Petersen graph is a\nthreefold Hopf-axis line $[u_{ij}]$.  Its $A_5$ setwise stabilizer has\norder six and is isomorphic to $S_3$; it permutes its three\nPetersen neighbors faithfully.  Its real permutation module splits\ncanonically as $\\mathbf1\\oplus W_{A_2}$, with\n\\[\n W_{A_2}=\\{(a,b,c)\\in\\mathbb R^3:a+b+c=0\\},\n \\qquad\\dim W_{A_2}=2.\n\\]\nWith a representative axis and compatible cyclic orientations, the\nPetersen cross-product directions $n_1,n_2,n_3\\in u_{ij}^{\\perp}$\nform an $A_2$ root trimer and the map\n$W_u=\\sqrt{2/3}\\,(n_1\\ n_2\\ n_3)$ satisfies\n\\[\n W_uW_u^{\\mathsf T}=I_3-u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\\mathsf T},\\qquad\n W_u^{\\mathsf T}W_u=I_3-\\tfrac13J_3.\n\\]\nThus the local trimer-defect plane is isometric to the transverse\nHopf/Clifford tangent plane, conditional on its labelled frame.\nThis is not an automatic identification with the earlier one-core\n$C_6^{\\rm link}$, its $\\mathbb C[Z_3]$ module, or the complex\nfundamental color representation.\n\\end{theorem}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2114,
          "end_line": 2124,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nThe stabilizer in $A_5$ of a two-label subset $\\{i,j\\}$ has\norder $60/10=6$; for every permutation of the three unused labels\nthere is a unique parity-compatible permutation of the selected pair.\nHence its action on the three unused two-label combinations is all\n$S_3$.  The permutation module decomposes into its constant\nline and its standard $A_2$ plane.  The transverse identities are\nthe exact vector-projector identities of Paper~I-A, and the map\nannihilates the constant line while preserving the inner product\non $W_{A_2}$.\n\\end{proof}"
        },
        "source_sha256": "1252358f75993d57fdd85038a1edbb345a22a1a613f87f1397eeba99d4ad6a8c",
        "statement_layer": "SOURCE-AS-PRINTED",
        "type_signature": "Ten Petersen local S3 fibres, A2 plane and transverse isometry",
        "quantifiers_and_conditions": "Occurring 2I packet; representative axis/compatible cyclic orientations for frame",
        "evidence_id": "IIE-B3-RG-0073",
        "evidence_level": "E1",
        "status_proposal": "REPRODUCED",
        "coverage": "E1_REPLAY_COMPLETED",
        "replay_steps": [

          "The A5 stabilizer of one two-subset has order 60/10=6. Every permutation of the three unused labels extends uniquely by a parity-compatible permutation of the selected pair, giving all six faithful neighbor permutations and hence S3.",

          "The three unit signed cross-product edge directions at the axis sum to zero and have mutual dot product -1/2. Their Gram is (3/2)I-(1/2)J.",

        ],

        "source_lines": [
          2126,
          2143
        ],
        "source_as_printed": "\\begin{proposition}[No global flat assignment of three edge colors]\n\\label{p2e:prop:v318-snark-no-flat-trimer}\nThe Petersen graph is not properly three-edge-colorable: its edge\nchromatic number is four.  Consequently its ten local three-channel\ntrimer fibres cannot all be identified with a single globally\nconstant three-color edge labelling.  This is a \\emph{flat labelling}\nobstruction, not a no-go theorem for a nontrivial local transition\nsystem, an $SU(3)$-valued color connection, or a physical color\nsinglet; each requires its own action/representation theorem.\n\\end{proposition}",
        "source_proof": {
          "start_line": 2136,
          "end_line": 2143,
          "text": "\\begin{proof}\nIn any three-edge-coloring of a cubic graph, one color is a\nperfect matching. Let\n\\(\\mathfrak M_{\\rm coord}(\\mathcal H_1)\\) be the family of Hermitian\n\\(\\operatorname{Sp}in(4)\\)-equivariant vector quadruples on \\(\\mathcal H_1\\) that match the\nnormalized scalar multiplication edge.         "source_excerpt": "\\]\nFor a unital star algebra, this compression preserves multiplication\nexactly if and only if $P$ reduces the algebra.\n\\end{lemma}\n\\begin{proof}\nInsert $ZZ^\\dagger=P$ between the two compressed factors. If the defect\nvanishes, take $B=A^\\dagger$: the positive matrix\n$Z^\\dagger A(I-P)A^\\dagger Z$ vanishes, so\n$(I-P)A^\\dagger Z=0$. Applying this to every $A$ and its adjoint proves\nreduction. The converse follows from $[P,A]=0$."

      "source_as_printed": "The factor \\(2\\) in both coefficients is\n\\(\\rank P_L=\\dim V_{(1/2,0)}=2\\), the complex chiral-spinor dimension of each\nprotected summand.  assert s.simplify(X[i]*X[3]-(a*a+b*b)*C[i]*C[3])==s.zeros(4)

 Y=[ai*c+bi*d for c,d in zip(C,D)]

 clifford_phase_controls.append([str(ai),str(bi)])

 assert A.det()==1
 th=A.conjugate().T.inv()
 for B in [A,th]:

# Invalid witnesses document why each is outside target hypotheses.

 return(a*e-b*f-c*g-d*h,a*f+b*e+c*h-d*g,a*g-b*h+c*e+d*f,a*h+b*g-c*f+d*e)

"""Exact exceptional-group moment/frontier controls for II-E's conditional atlas.
This is mathematical evidence only; group/role occurrence is not inferred.
"""
from itertools import product,permutations
from fractions import Fraction as F
from math import factorial
import json
from pathlib import Path
checks=[]
def ok(n,c,r):
 if not c: raise AssertionError(n)
 checks.append({'check':n,'passed':True,'result':r})

# Q(sqrt5) coordinates in the basis (1,sqrt5), represented as rational pairs.
def add(x,y): return (x[0]+y[0],x[1]+y[1])
def mul(x,y): return (x[0]*y[0]+5*x[1]*y[1],x[0]*y[1]+x[1]*y[0])
def neg(x): return (-x[0],-x[1])
def scale(x,c): return (x[0]*c,x[1]*c)
def pw(x,n):
 r=(F(1),F(0))
 for _ in range(n):r=mul(r,x)
 return r
zero=(F(0),F(0));one=(F(1),F(0));half=(F(1,2),F(0))
phi2=(F(1,4),F(1,4));invphi2=(F(-1,4),F(1,4))
T=[]
for j in range(4):
 for sign in [-1,1]:
  q=[zero]*4;q[j]=scale(one,sign);T.append(tuple(q))
T += [tuple(scale(half,v) for v in signs) for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=4)]
Is=set(T)
for per in permutations(range(4)):
 if sum(per[i]>per[j] for i in range(4) for j in range(i+1,4))%2:continue
 for signs in product([-1,1],repeat=3):
  v=[zero]+[scale(x,y) for x,y in zip([half,phi2,invphi2],signs)]
  Is.add(tuple(v[j] for j in per))
Is=sorted(Is)
ok('Icosahedral coordinate count',len(Is)==120,{'count':len(Is)})

# Even-coordinate moments of 2O are rational because the added vertices have
# exactly two nonzero coordinates of magnitude 1/sqrt2. Their odd moments
# vanish by independent sign reversals, as for the two other coordinate sets.
O_sq=[tuple(F(x[0]*x[0]+5*x[1]*x[1]) for x in q) for q in T]
for i in range(4):
 for j in range(i+1,4):
  for _ in range(4):
   q=[F(0)]*4;q[i]=q[j]=F(1,2);O_sq.append(tuple(q))
T_sq=[tuple(mul(x,x) for x in q) for q in T]
I_sq=[tuple(mul(x,x) for x in q) for q in Is]
def haar(es):
 n=sum(es)
 return F(__import__('functools').reduce(lambda a,b:a*b,(factorial(2*k)//factorial(k) for k in es),1),4**n*factorial(n+1))
def avg_ext(sq,es):
 acc=zero
 for q in sq:
  v=one
  for x,n in zip(q,es):v=mul(v,pw(x,n))
  acc=add(acc,v)
 return scale(acc,F(1,len(sq)))
def avg_rat(sq,es):return sum((__import__('functools').reduce(lambda a,b:a*b,(x**n for x,n in zip(q,es)),F(1)) for q in sq),F(0))/len(sq)
for name,sq,limit,external in [('2T',T_sq,2,True),('2O',O_sq,3,False),('2I',I_sq,5,True)]:
 count=0
 for es in product(range(limit+1),repeat=4):
  if sum(es)>limit:continue
  h=haar(es);v=avg_ext(sq,es) if external else (avg_rat(sq,es),F(0))
  ok(name+' even moment '+str(es),v==(h,F(0)),{'exponents':str(tuple(2*n for n in es)),'value':str(h)})
  count+=1
 checks.append({'check':name+' design summary','passed':True,'result':{'even_monomials':count,'odd_moments':'zero by coordinate sign symmetry','degree_strength':2*limit+1}})
for name,sq,n,external in [('2T',T_sq,3,True),('2O',O_sq,4,False),('2I',I_sq,6,True)]:
 es=(n,0,0,0);v=avg_ext(sq,es) if external else (avg_rat(sq,es),F(0));h=haar(es)
 ok(name+' first failed even moment',v!=(h,F(0)),{'finite':str(v[0]),'haar':str(h),'degree':2*n})

# Independently enumerate A5 and its five vertex stabilizers. These are the
# projective tetrahedral cores; each pair intersects in a cyclic order-three
# subgroup, whose binary lift is order six.
def parity(p):return sum(p[i]>p[j] for i in range(len(p)) for j in range(i+1,len(p)))%2
def comp(p,q):return tuple(p[q[j]] for j in range(len(p)))
def inv(p):return tuple(p.index(j) for j in range(len(p)))
A5=[p for p in permutations(range(5)) if parity(p)==0]
cores=[{p for p in A5 if p[j]==j} for j in range(5)]
sizes=[len(cores[i]&cores[j]) for i in range(5) for j in range(i+1,5)]
ok('Five projective tetrahedral cores',len(A5)==60 and all(len(c)==12 for c in cores) and sizes==[3]*10,{'A5_order':60,'cores':5,'core_orders':[12]*5,'pairwise_intersection_orders':sizes})

# Matrix presentation controls for abstract scalar torsion automorphisms.
def mm(A,B,p):return tuple(sum(A[2*i+k]*B[2*k+j] for k in range(2))%p for i in range(2) for j in range(2))
def mp(A,n,p):
 r=(1,0,0,1)
 for _ in range(n):r=mm(r,A,p)
 return r
def gen(gs,p):
 seen={(1,0,0,1)};todo=list(seen)
 while todo:
  a=todo.pop()
  for b in gs:
   c=mm(a,b,p)
   if c not in seen:seen.add(c);todo.append(c)
 return seen
for p in [3,5]:
 allm={a for a in product(range(p),repeat=4) if (a[0]*a[3]-a[1]*a[2])%p==1}
 A=(0,p-1,1,0);B=(0,p-1,1,1);minus=(p-1,0,0,p-1)
 G=gen([A,B],p)
 ok('Scalar SL2F'+str(p)+' binary triangle presentation',G==allm and mp(A,2,p)==minus and mp(B,3,p)==minus and mp(mm(A,B,p),p,p)==minus,{'order':len(G),'A_squared':'-I','B_cubed':'-I','AB_power':p,'AB_power_value':'-I'})

out={'kind':'E3-INDEPENDENT-EXACT','target_label':'p2e:thm:joint-exceptional-core-support-ledger','lineage':'Explicit exceptional quaternion coordinate moments; permutation A5 stabilizers; finite SL2 fields. No occurrence status imported.','checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':True,'checks':checks}
Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
print(json.dumps({'checks_count':len(checks),'all_passed':True}))

basis=[I2]+pauli; metric=s.diag(1,-1,-1,-1)
for n,A in enumerate(As):

    ok('Lorentz congruence control '+str(n),s.simplify(T.T*metric*T)==metric and s.simplify(T.det())==1 and T[0,0]>0,{'T':str(T)})
    H=s.Matrix([[2,1-I],[1+I,3]])
    theta=A.conjugate().T.inv()
    dual=s.simplify(s.trace(theta*H*A.inv()*A*K*A.conjugate().T)/2-s.trace(H*K)/2)

# is checked over R, including its pseudoscalar, rather than assumed from the

e=[C[i]*C[3] for i in range(3)]
mons=[I4]+e+[e[i]*e[j] for i in range(3) for j in range(i+1,3)]+[e[0]*e[1]*e[2]]
